laws.rule: You must always be able to show an official form of ID such as your passport. The police will usually accept a printed copy.
laws.heading: Personal ID

laws.rule: Possession or trafficking of drugs is a serious offence in Kiribati, and prison sentences may be heavy.
laws.heading: Illegal drugs and prison sentences

laws.rule: You should respect local customs about dress, including swimming costumes. Local laws ban public nudity and revealing swimming costumes.
laws.heading: Public nudity

laws.rule: Same-sex sexual acts are illegal. If found guilty, the penalty could be up to 14 years imprisonment. Read more advice for LGBT+ travellers .
laws.heading: LGBT+ travellers

laws.rule: Internet and mobile phone services are available in some parts of Kiribati. Not all of the outer islands are connected. Services can be unreliable and expensive because of the country’s remote location.
laws.heading: Internet and phone services

laws.rule: Stray dogs have bitten visitors. Be cautious, particularly on the beach. If a dog approaches you, do not run. Reaching down as if to pick up something off the ground can be enough to scare dogs away. If a dog bites you, seek medical attention immediately.
laws.heading: Stray dogs

laws.rule: Very few places accept credit cards in Kiribati. There are ATMs at branches of the Bank of Kiribati and ANZ in Betio, Bairiki and Bikenibeu on Tarawa atoll.
laws.heading: Money
